Kenji López-Alt Aug 12, 2026 View in app View in app Bento boxes and bullet trains go hand in hand in more ways than one: Follow along as we enjoy a taste test and trace the history of these iconic symbols of Japan. Content & Community Manager Erin here to introduce this episode of Kenji Eats Japan: Bento Boxes on a Bullet Train. Join Kenji and Akari to dive into bento culture and explore some of the common food offerings you might find at a Japanese train station. Bento boxes and bullet trains are two of the most iconic symbols of modern day Japan. But where did either of them come from, and how are they connected? Let’s dive in. Bento Box History: I’d argue, the evolution of bento boxes reflects the evolution of Japan as a nation. Their origins are simple and straightforward, with iterations of bento boxes appearing as early as the Kamakura period and continuing to evolve through the Edo period as an easy way to bring food to work, school, or cultural events. ¹ It was during the Meiji era—a period of rapid industrialization and modernization that began in 1868—that bento boxes naturally took off...
